validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Reproduced end-to-end in a real browser against $PREVIEW_URL, and the mechanism was confirmed by a scratch vitest run that reproduced the row-axis construction directly through categoryLists/groupBySelections with the exact inputs CustomReport.tsx passes. What is below 100 is the fix's blast radius, not the diagnosis: custom-spreadsheet.ts and grouped-spreadsheet.ts build the axis independently, GetCardData.tsx is a second caller that I could not exercise in the browser within this run, and the interaction with payee/account splits (which share the same axis-building code but take a different branch) was reasoned about rather than observed.
validated_work_order.understanding: Reproduced exactly as reported, on the demo budget at $PREVIEW_URL, headless Chromium 1.61.1. Steps: open /reports/custom (fresh Custom Report, Mode=Total, Split=Category, Type=Payment, Interval=Monthly), click 'Data Table' in the topbar, click 'Unselect All' in the category selector, tick only the 'Bills' group checkbox, then Options -> 'Show empty rows'. With Show empty rows OFF the table correctly shows only the five Bills categories (Cell, Internet, Mortgage, Water, Power) totalling -3,050.00. Turning 'Show empty rows' ON adds back every unchecked category in the entire budget at 0.00: the 'Usual Expenses' group with Food, Restaurants, Entertainment, Clothing, General, Gift, Medical and Savings; the 'Income' group with Starting Balances, Misc and Income; and 'Uncategorized & Off budget' with Uncategorized, Transfers and Off budget. The applied filter chip reads 'category one of [Cell, Internet, Mortgage, 2 more items...]', so the selection is correctly recorded and correctly applied to the amounts - only the row axis is wrong. I also varied the selection away from a whole group, since the reporter's phrasing ('only selecting a category group') could have implied a group-specific defect: ticking a single category instead ('Food' only) produces the same symptom, with Restaurants, Entertainment and Clothing appearing at 0.00. The bug is therefore in the selection filter generally, not in group handling. Console output during the reproduction carried no errors and no failed requests beyond two pre-existing React duplicate-key warnings ('Encountered two children with the same key'), which are present on the unmodified page before any of my steps and are unrelated to this bug.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The report's category selection is applied only to the amounts, never to the row axis. CustomReport.tsx derives `selectedCategories` from the filter conditions (line 267) and hands it to ReportSidebar to render the checkboxes, but the two spreadsheet factories are called with the raw `categories` object from useCategories() (lines 519 and 555), which is every category in the budget. createCustomSpreadsheet then calls categoryLists(categories) -> groupBySelections(...) to build groupByList, and that list is the set of rows the report will ever render; createGroupedSpreadsheet does the same via categoryLists(categories) to build its per-group rows. Meanwhile the selection reaches the amounts only as a `category oneOf [...]` query filter, applied inside fetchSpreadsheetQueryData/makeQuery, so an unselected category correctly contributes 0 to every amount. The row and the amount therefore disagree. filterEmptyRows is the only thing that ever reconciled them, and it does so destructively: when showEmpty is false it drops every zero row, which coincidentally also drops the unselected categories and hides the defect; when showEmpty is true it returns true unconditionally, so all the unselected rows survive at 0.00. `Show empty rows` is thus not overriding the selection - it is removing the only filter that was hiding the fact that the selection never reached the axis. Note the same asymmetry already has a correct implementation elsewhere: fetchBudgetData (the Type=Budgeted path) calls filterCategoriesByConditions to narrow its category list before use, which is why the axis and the amounts agree there.
validated_work_order.approach: Narrow the category axis at the point the spreadsheets build it, using the existing filterCategoriesByConditions helper in budgetDataQuery.ts rather than a new filter. Concretely: in custom-spreadsheet.ts and grouped-spreadsheet.ts, derive an effective category list/group list from `categories` filtered through filterCategoriesByConditions(categories.list, categories.grouped, conditions, conditionsOp) and pass that narrowed set to categoryLists/groupBySelections instead of the unfiltered `categories`. Keep passing the unfiltered `categories.list` to fetchSpreadsheetQueryData, so the query-side filter is untouched and the two sides are computed from the same expression. Reuse filterCategoriesByConditions deliberately rather than writing a narrower predicate: it already understands 'category' and 'category_group' fields, is/oneOf/notOneOf/isNot, and the contains/matches text operators, and - importantly - it already returns the input unfiltered when it cannot safely interpret a condition (isSupportedCategoryCondition guard). That conservative fallback is what keeps complex conditions (the ones CustomReport.tsx already flags via isComplexCategoryCondition) behaving exactly as they do today rather than silently dropping rows. Keep filterEmptyRows unchanged; it is correct for its job and is only ever exposed by this bug. Do not special-case groupBy - the defect is upstream of the split, in the shared axis, so fixing it in categoryLists' callers fixes Payee, Account, Group, Category and Interval splits at once.

Step 2 - clicked 'Data Table' in the topbar to reach table view.

Mechanism confirmed by a scratch vitest run (packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/__mech.test.ts, since deleted) driving the exact axis-construction path custom-spreadsheet.ts uses - categoryLists(categories) followed by groupBySelections('Category', ...) - with the exact inputs CustomReport.tsx passes (the full useCategories() list: Food and Rent in g-usual, Cell in g-bills, plus both groups). Command: yarn workspace @actual-app/web exec vitest run src/components/reports/spreadsheets/__mech.test.ts. Result: 1 passed, with the console logging the row axis as [Food, Rent, Cell, Uncategorized, Off budget, Transfers] - i.e. the axis contains both unchecked categories, confirming the axis is built from the unfiltered list and that the selection never reaches it. This is what distinguishes a logic bug (wrong store) from a render bug (correct store, stale DOM): the amounts in the table are correct and only the row set is wrong.

Console/network during the reproduction: no errors attributable to this bug and no failed requests. The only console errors were two instances of React's 'Encountered two children with the same key' warning, which reproduce on the untouched page before any of my interactions and are pre-existing and unrelated.

Code corroboration, read after the reproduction: CustomReport.tsx:267 computes `selectedCategories` from the filter conditions and passes it only to ReportSidebar (line 894) for rendering the checkboxes, while createGroupedSpreadsheet (line 519) and createCustomSpreadsheet (line 555) both receive the raw unfiltered `categories` from useCategories() (line 152). custom-spreadsheet.ts:87-92 builds groupByList from that unfiltered list via categoryLists/groupBySelections, and that list is the complete set of rows the report can ever render. The selection reaches the amounts only as a query filter inside makeQuery (makeQuery.ts:26-28) via fetchSpreadsheetQueryData, so unselected categories correctly contribute 0 - the row and the amount disagree by construction. filterEmptyRows (filterEmptyRows.ts:24) is the only thing that ever hid this: `return !showEmpty ? showHide : true` drops zero rows when showEmpty is off, incidentally dropping the unselected categories too.

Corroborating asymmetry found in the same flow: the Type=Budgeted path already does this correctly. fetchSpreadsheetQueryData routes totalBudgeted to fetchBudgetData, which calls filterCategoriesByConditions (budgetDataQuery.ts) to narrow the category list before building anything. That helper is the correct, already-tested implementation of exactly the narrowing this fix needs, and it already carries the conservative 'cannot safely interpret -> do not filter' fallback. Reusing it is why the approach does not invent a second predicate.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix it inside filterEmptyRows - make showEmpty-aware filtering also drop rows belonging to unselected categories.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That treats the symptom. filterEmptyRows only sees a GroupedEntity and its flag; it has no knowledge of the selection conditions, so honouring the selection there would mean threading the whole condition set through a function whose job is a zero/nonzero test. It would also leave the axis itself wrong - every unselected category would still be computed, summed into totals and handed to the legend and the graph on every render, and any other consumer of the axis (legend, graph, snapshot) would keep seeing the phantom rows. The debugger rule is to fix what produces the bad value, and the bad value is the row axis.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix it in CustomReport.tsx by passing selectedCategories into the spreadsheet factories instead of the full categories.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Tempting and much smaller, but wrong in two ways. First, useSelectedCategories (CustomReport.tsx:73-113) only understands a 'category' field with is/isNot/oneOf/notOneOf and deliberately returns the FULL list for every other condition shape - including category_group conditions, text operators, and the multiple-category-condition case that isComplexCategoryCondition exists to flag. So this would narrow the axis for simple selections and silently do nothing for the complex ones, an inconsistency users would hit and could not explain. Second, categories.grouped is still needed for the Group split and for per-group rows, so the prop would have to be split in two anyway. Reusing filterCategoriesByConditions handles both condition shapes with one already-tested expression.

alternatives_considered.approach: Filter inside categoryLists() in ReportOptions.ts, since both factories call it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: categoryLists takes only { list, grouped } and no conditions, so filtering there would require changing its signature to accept the conditions - turning a pure shape helper into one that silently drops rows based on a second input. Its existing sibling callers and its single-responsibility shape (build the three axis lists plus the synthetic Uncategorized/Off budget/Transfers rows) would be lost, and the unit tests for it would have to grow condition fixtures. Narrowing at the two factories that own the spreadsheet inputs keeps the helper pure and puts the change where the two callers can share one expression.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add the row filter as a new, narrower predicate local to custom-spreadsheet.ts, handling only the category oneOf/is/isNot/notOneOf shape.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Duplicates filterCategoriesByConditions, which already implements exactly this and is already covered by budgetDataQuery.test.ts (category, category_group, oneOf, text operators, combined and/or). A second predicate would drift from it and would have no equivalent of its 'cannot safely interpret -> do not filter' guard, which is the safety property that keeps complex-condition reports from silently losing rows.

risks: Over-narrowing is the real hazard. filterCategoriesByConditions returns the input unfiltered when it cannot safely interpret a condition, and that fallback is load-bearing: it is what keeps reports using complex category conditions (the isComplexCategoryCondition set in CustomReport.tsx - multiple category conditions, category_group conditions, contains/doesNotContain/matches/hasTags/hasAnyTag) rendering every row they render today. The new tests must pin that fallback explicitly (AC-4), or the fix trades one wrong report for a worse one.

Two files change, and the second is not optional. In Split=Category the table renders data.groupedData (ReportTableList.tsx:28-31), which comes from createGroupedSpreadsheet. Fixing only custom-spreadsheet.ts would fix the bar/line/donut charts and leave the reporter's exact table-view symptom fully intact. An implementer who changes one file will see graphs corrected and the table still wrong, and may conclude the fix failed.

Two callers exist and both are affected. GetCardData.tsx (lines 127 and 146) calls the same two factories for dashboard report widgets, passing its own `categories` prop. Because the fix lives inside the factories, dashboard widgets are corrected by the same change and need no edit - but that also means this change alters dashboard widget output, which is outside what the reporter described. It is the correct behaviour (a widget showing a filtered report should not render unselected rows), and the shared-function argument is what makes it right, but it should be a conscious acceptance rather than a surprise at review.

The Budgeted path shares the helper. Type=Budgeted already narrowed its own axis inside fetchBudgetData; both axes now run through filterCategoriesByConditions. The narrowing is applied to the axis only, and the query call is left on the unfiltered categories, so Budgeted's data path is untouched - but AC-7 exists to confirm this empirically rather than by argument.

Low-confidence residual: I verified the Payment/Deposit/Net types and Split=Category in the browser. I did not separately observe the Payee, Account and Interval splits, which share the same axis-construction code but take different branches of groupBySelections, and I did not exercise the dashboard-widget path (GetCardData.tsx) in a browser within this run. Those follow from the shared fix rather than from separate observation, and AC-6 is written to check them structurally.
out_of_scope: The synthetic Uncategorized / Off budget / Transfers rows that categoryLists always appends. They appeared at 0.00 in the reproduction, but they are appended unconditionally by design (ReportOptions.ts:398-400, 403-406) and are governed by the showUncategorized and showOffBudget flags, not by the category selection. Whether the synthetic block should respect showEmpty differently is a separate question and changing it would alter behaviour for reports that are not filtered at all.

The two React 'Encountered two children with the same key' console warnings. They reproduce on the untouched page before any interaction, so they are pre-existing and unrelated to this bug - filing them here would bury this fix.

Renaming the user-facing string 'Show empty rows'. The reporter called it 'show unused rows', but the label in the running app is 'Show empty rows' and matches its tooltip ('Show rows that are zero or blank'). The label is accurate; only the interaction with selection is wrong.
The `Sort` control defaulting to 'Budget' rather than 'Descending' in the reproduction. Noted while observing the sidebar; unrelated to this defect and not investigated.
assumptions: The fix belongs in the shared axis construction rather than in Split=Category specifically. This is inferred from the code path (both factories call the same categoryLists helper) and from the single-category variation reproducing identically, not from observing every split in the browser.

filterCategoriesByConditions is the intended narrowing helper. Its semantics match what is needed - it understands both condition fields and carries the conservative fallback - and its existing use on the Budgeted path shows the codebase already treats it as the canonical answer to this question. If a maintainer prefers a different helper, the diagnosis and the reproduction still hold; only the approach would change.

Passing the unfiltered categories to fetchSpreadsheetQueryData while narrowing only the axis is correct, because the query needs the full list to evaluate the condition itself. This follows from makeQuery applying the conditions as a filter.
unknowns: Whether unchecking a category has always produced this, or whether it is a regression. git history here is a single squashed import commit ('Import actualbudget/actual at 3ef90fe'), so git log -S and git blame cannot date the change or reveal its original intent. The upstream issue reports it as filed 2024-10-14 and still open, which suggests long-standing rather than recent, but that is the reporter's account, not something the repository confirms.

Whether maintainers would want unselected categories hidden, or want the empty rows limited to the selected group. The reporter's intent is unambiguous - 'even show empty rows in that group' - and hiding unselected rows is the only reading consistent with the sidebar's 'Hide unchecked' control, but the exact intended boundary for the synthetic Uncategorized/Off budget block is not stated anywhere in the ticket.
